title.en: Routing: datagrams or virtual circuits, and distance vector (Q9, Q10)
title.zh: 路由：数据报还是虚电路，以及距离向量（第 9、10 题）

description.en: How a connectionless and a connection-oriented network layer route packets and what each costs; how a router builds its routes from its neighbours' distance vectors, worked through question 10's network.
description.zh: 无连接和面向连接的网络层各怎样为分组选路、各有什么代价；路由器怎样根据邻居的距离向量算出自己的路由，用第 10 题的网络完整算一遍。

name.zh: 无连接服务与数据报子网 (connectionless service, datagram subnet)
面向连接服务与虚电路子网 (connection-oriented service, virtual-circuit subnet)
数据报与虚电路的比较 (datagram vs virtual-circuit subnets)
距离向量路由 (distance vector routing)
链路状态路由 (link state routing)

description.en: Thinking a virtual circuit reserves a wire of its own
description.zh: 以为虚电路独占一条线路

description.en: Computing a router's new vector from its own old distances instead of its neighbours' vectors
description.zh: 用路由器自己的旧距离，而不是邻居的向量，来算新向量

title.zh: 模拟卷 · 第 9 题（4 分）

paras.en: With respect to routing packets in the Network Layer, explain the difference between connectionless and connection-oriented services?
paras.zh: 就网络层中分组的路由而言，说明无连接服务和面向连接服务的区别。

items.en: **The network layer** carries packets from the source host to the destination host across a chain of routers.
items.zh: **网络层**把分组从源主机经过一连串路由器送到目的主机。

items.en: **Connectionless**: nothing is set up before the packets are sent. **Connection-oriented**: a connection is set up first, and the packets then use it.
items.zh: **无连接**：发分组之前什么都不建立。**面向连接**：先建立一条连接，分组再沿着它走。

items.en: **With respect to routing packets**: the question is about how the route of each packet is chosen, and what that means for the routers, not about reliability in the transport layer.
items.zh: **就分组的路由而言**：问的是每个分组的路线怎么选，以及这对路由器意味着什么，不是传输层的可靠性。

items.en: **4 marks**: two bullets, each saying how that service routes packets, plus the contrasts that follow from it.
items.zh: **4 分**：两条要点，各说明这种服务怎样给分组选路，再加由此引出的对比。

chapter.zh: 第 9 题：数据报还是虚电路

title.en: Each packet on its own, or all along one path
title.zh: 每个分组各走各的，还是都走同一条路

text.en: Routers work by **store-and-forward**: a router receives a whole packet, stores it, and sends it on along the next link towards its destination. The question is how a router decides that next link.
text.zh: 路由器的工作方式是**存储转发**：收下一个完整的分组，存起来，再沿着通往目的地的下一条链路发出去。问题是：路由器怎么决定下一条链路？

alt.en: Two copies of a four-router network. Datagram: packets 1 and 3 go A, B, D and packets 2 and 4 go A, C, D. Virtual circuit: packets 1 to 4 all go A, B, D on circuit VC 7.
alt.zh: 同一个四台路由器的网络画了两份。数据报：分组 1 和 3 走 A、B、D，分组 2 和 4 走 A、C、D。虚电路：分组 1 到 4 都在虚电路 VC 7 上走 A、B、D。

caption.en: Left: every datagram is looked up on its own, so packets of one message can take different paths. Right: a virtual circuit is set up once, and every packet follows it.
caption.zh: 左：每个数据报单独查表，同一条消息的分组可能走不同的路。右：虚电路建立一次，之后每个分组都沿着它走。

items.en: **Connectionless: a datagram network** (the course calls it the post office model). Each packet, a **datagram**, carries the full destination address. Every router looks the address up in its routing table, as in question 7, and forwards the packet. Nothing is set up first, and each packet is routed independently: if a table changes, later packets take another path and may arrive out of order. The Internet's IP works this way.
items.zh: **无连接：数据报网络**（课上叫邮局模式）。每个分组叫一个**数据报**（datagram），带着完整的目的地址。每台路由器在自己的路由表里查这个地址（就像第 7 题那样），再转发出去。事先什么都不建立，每个分组独立选路：路由表一变，后面的分组就走别的路，到达顺序也可能乱。互联网的 IP 就是这样工作的。

items.en: **Connection-oriented: a virtual-circuit network** (the telephone model). Before any data, a path from the source router to the destination router is set up, a **virtual circuit**, and every router on it records the circuit in a table: *arriving on this line with this circuit number, send out on that line with that number*. Packets then carry only a short circuit number and all follow the same path, in order. MPLS inside ISP networks works this way.
items.zh: **面向连接：虚电路网络**（电话模式）。发数据之前，先从源路由器到目的路由器建好一条路径，叫**虚电路**（virtual circuit），路径上每台路由器都在表里记下这条电路：*从这条线、带这个电路号进来的，从那条线、换那个号出去*。之后分组只带一个短短的电路号，全都沿同一条路按顺序走。ISP 网络内部的 MPLS 就是这样工作的。

text.en: A virtual circuit is *virtual*: it is a row in each router's table, not a wire. The links are still shared with all other traffic.
text.zh: 虚电路是*虚*的：它只是每台路由器表里的一行，不是一根线。链路照样和其他所有流量共用。

rows.en: full destination address in every packet
rows.zh: 每个分组带完整目的地址

rows.en: a short VC number in every packet
rows.zh: 每个分组带一个短的电路号

rows.en: route chosen once, at setup; all packets follow it
rows.zh: 建立时选一次路，所有分组都沿它走

rows.en: a table for every possible destination; no per-connection state
rows.zh: 一张覆盖所有目的地的表；不记连接

rows.en: one entry per circuit through it
rows.zh: 经过它的每条电路一项

rows.en: a longer lookup for every packet
setup time, then very fast forwarding
rows.zh: 要花建立时间，之后转发很快

rows.en: every circuit through it is lost and must be rebuilt
rows.zh: 经过它的电路全部中断，必须重建

rows.en: easy: resources can be reserved at setup
rows.zh: 容易：建立时可以预留资源

text.en: The two communities behind them explain the choice, as the course puts it: the Internet community wanted to move packets over a possibly unreliable network and leave flow and error control to other layers; the telecommunications community wanted guaranteed reliability and quality of service.
text.zh: 课上说，两种设计背后是两个群体的不同取向：互联网群体想在可能不可靠的网络上把分组送过去，流量和差错控制交给别的层；电信群体要的是有保证的可靠性和服务质量。

prompt.en: A router on the path of several virtual circuits crashes. What happens to them?
prompt.zh: 一台路由器位于好几条虚电路的路径上，它崩溃了。这些电路会怎样？

label.en: Their packets are routed around it automatically
label.zh: 它们的分组会自动绕过它

feedback.en: That is what datagrams do. A circuit's path is fixed at setup, so its packets have nowhere else to go.
feedback.zh: 那是数据报的做法。电路的路径在建立时就定了，分组没有别的路可走。

label.en: Every circuit through it is aborted and has to be set up again
label.zh: 经过它的每条电路都中断了，必须重新建立

label.en: Nothing: the circuit's wire is reserved in advance
label.zh: 没事：电路的线路是事先预留好的

feedback.en: A virtual circuit is an entry in each router's table, not a wire; the crashed router's entries are gone.
feedback.zh: 虚电路是每台路由器表里的一项，不是一根线；崩溃的路由器里的表项全没了。

explain.en: The circuit lives in the routers' tables. When a router on the path fails, the circuits through it are lost, and no traffic flows on them until they are rebuilt.
explain.zh: 电路存在于各路由器的表里。路径上的一台路由器坏了，经过它的电路就没了，重建之前这些电路上没有流量。

text.en: Two bullets, each with how it routes and what follows: no setup and independent routing against a path set up first; the full address against a circuit number; rerouting around failures against circuits lost.
text.zh: 两条要点，每条写它怎样选路、由此带来什么：不建立、独立选路，对比先建好一条路径；完整地址，对比电路号；故障时绕路，对比电路中断。

title.en: Practice exam, Q9 · a full-mark answer
title.zh: 模拟卷第 9 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Connectionless (datagram) service: no connection is set up in advance. Packets are injected into the network individually; each carries the full destination address and is routed independently of the others, so packets of the same message may take different paths and arrive out of order. Routers keep no per-connection state, and if a router fails, packets can be routed around it.
paras.zh: 无连接（数据报）服务：事先不建立连接。分组被逐个注入网络；每个分组带完整的目的地址，与其他分组无关地独立选路，所以同一条消息的分组可能走不同的路径、乱序到达。路由器不保存每条连接的状态，某台路由器故障时，分组可以绕过它。

paras.en: Connection-oriented (virtual-circuit) service: a path from the source router all the way to the destination router must be established before any data packets are sent; this connection is called a virtual circuit. Each router on the path records the circuit, packets carry only a short circuit identifier, and all of them follow the same path in order. Setup takes time and router state, and a router failure breaks every circuit through it, but quality of service is easier to provide.
paras.zh: 面向连接（虚电路）服务：在发送任何数据分组之前，必须先建立一条从源路由器一直到目的路由器的路径，这条连接称为虚电路。路径上每台路由器都记录这条电路，分组只携带一个短的电路标识，并且全部按顺序沿同一路径走。建立需要时间和路由器状态，路由器故障会中断经过它的所有电路，但更容易提供服务质量保证。

title.zh: 模拟卷 · 第 10 题（6 分）

paras.en: Distance vector routing is used for a network of six nodes as shown below.
paras.zh: 一个由六个节点组成的网络（如下图）使用距离向量路由。

paras.en: The following vectors have just come into router C from B: (5, 0, 7, 11, 10, 7); from D: (15, 11, 4, 0, 10, 11); and from E: (5, 10, 6, 10, 0, 3). Each vector contains the distances from a certain node to the other nodes, in the order of (A, B, C, D, E, F). The distances from C to B, D, and E, are 7, 4, and 6, respectively.
paras.zh: 路由器 C 刚收到以下向量：来自 B 的 (5, 0, 7, 11, 10, 7)；来自 D 的 (15, 11, 4, 0, 10, 11)；来自 E 的 (5, 10, 6, 10, 0, 3)。每个向量按 (A, B, C, D, E, F) 的顺序给出某个节点到其他各节点的距离。C 到 B、D、E 的距离分别是 7、4、6。

paras.en: What is the new vector for C? Show a table of the outgoing lines to use and the expected distances from C to all the other nodes.
paras.zh: C 的新向量是什么？列一张表，写出 C 到其他各节点应使用的出口线路和预计距离。

chapter.zh: 第 10 题：距离向量路由

text.en: No router sees the whole network. In **distance vector routing** each router keeps a table of the lowest known distance to every destination and the line used to get there. It knows the distance to each of its neighbours, and periodically it sends its vector to them. When the vectors arrive, it recomputes every entry: for each destination, try each neighbour, add the length of the link to that neighbour to the distance the neighbour reports, and keep the smallest sum. The neighbour that gave it is the outgoing line. The course's phrase: global information, shared locally.
text.zh: 没有一台路由器能看见整个网络。在**距离向量路由**里，每台路由器有一张表，记着到每个目的地已知的最短距离，以及走哪条线。它知道到每个邻居的距离，并定期把自己的向量发给邻居。向量一到，它就把每一项重算一遍：对每个目的地，逐个试邻居，把到这个邻居的链路长度加上邻居报来的距离，留下最小的和。给出这个最小值的邻居，就是出口线路。课上的说法：全局的信息，在局部交换。

text.en: Here $D_C(X)$ is C's new distance to destination $X$, $c(C, N)$ the length of C's link to neighbour $N$, and $D_N(X)$ the distance $N$ reported. It is right because of the course's **optimality principle**: if C's best path to A goes through E, the rest of it is E's best path to A, so E's reported distance is exactly what C needs.
text.zh: 其中 $D_C(X)$ 是 C 到目的地 $X$ 的新距离，$c(C, N)$ 是 C 到邻居 $N$ 的链路长度，$D_N(X)$ 是 $N$ 报来的距离。这样算是对的，依据是课上的**最优性原理**：如果 C 到 A 的最佳路径经过 E，那么这条路径剩下的部分就是 E 到 A 的最佳路径，所以 E 报来的距离正是 C 需要的。

title.zh: 距离向量对比链路状态

text.en: Distance vector has a known weakness, which the course gives as its reason for the alternative: it takes too long to converge after the network changes. Good news spreads quickly, one hop per exchange. Bad news spreads slowly. If a link fails, the neighbours still advertise routes that went through it, each router believes the others, and the distances creep up one exchange at a time: the **count-to-infinity** problem.
text.zh: 距离向量有个出名的弱点，课上正是拿它来引出另一种算法：网络一变，它要很久才能收敛。好消息传得快，每交换一次往前走一跳。坏消息传得慢。一条链路断了，邻居们还在通告经过它的路由，每台路由器都相信别人，距离每交换一次才往上涨一点：这就是**无穷计数**（count-to-infinity）问题。

text.en: **Link state routing** shares the information the other way round: local information, shared globally. Each router measures the distance to each neighbour, puts them in a **link state packet**, and floods it to every router. Every router then holds the whole map and computes its own shortest paths with Dijkstra's algorithm. It needs more computation and memory, but it converges quickly; OSPF, widely used on the Internet, works this way.
text.zh: **链路状态路由**反过来分享信息：局部的信息，全局地分享。每台路由器测量到各邻居的距离，写进一个**链路状态分组**，再泛洪给所有路由器。于是每台路由器都有整张地图，自己用 Dijkstra 算法算最短路径。它要更多的计算和内存，但收敛快；互联网上广泛使用的 OSPF 就是这样工作的。

title.en: Your turn: a worse route through E
title.zh: 你来：经 E 的路变差了

prompt.en: Suppose E's vector had said its distance to F is 12 instead of 3, with everything else as in the question. What is C's new route to F?
prompt.zh: 假设 E 的向量里，它到 F 的距离是 12 而不是 3，其余都和题目一样。C 到 F 的新路由是什么？

feedback.en: C does not keep its old entries: the new vector is built from the fresh vectors alone, and E now offers $6 + 12 = 18$.
feedback.zh: C 不保留旧的表项：新向量只用刚收到的向量来算，而 E 现在给出的是 $6 + 12 = 18$。

feedback.en: Through E is now the worst of the three: B offers $7 + 7 = 14$.
feedback.zh: 经 E 现在是三条里最差的：B 给出的是 $7 + 7 = 14$。

title.en: Your turn: two packets, two paths

prompt.en: Two packets of the same message reach the destination by different paths, the second before the first. Which network layer service allows this?
prompt.zh: 同一条消息的两个分组走不同的路到达目的地，第二个比第一个先到。哪种网络层服务会出现这种情况？

feedback.en: On a virtual circuit every packet follows the path set up at the start, in order.
feedback.zh: 在虚电路上，每个分组都沿着一开始建好的路径按顺序走。

explain.en: Each datagram is routed independently, so when a table changes between them, they can take different paths and overtake each other.
explain.zh: 每个数据报独立选路，两个分组之间路由表一变，它们就可能走不同的路，后发的还可能先到。

prompt.en: In which routing algorithm does every router learn the whole network map and compute its own shortest paths?
prompt.zh: 在哪种路由算法里，每台路由器都知道整张网络图，并自己计算最短路径？

feedback.en: A distance vector router knows only its neighbours and their vectors, never the map.
feedback.zh: 距离向量的路由器只知道邻居和邻居的向量，从来看不到整张图。

explain.en: Link state floods every router's link costs to all routers, and each runs Dijkstra on the full map.
explain.zh: 链路状态把每台路由器的链路长度泛洪给所有路由器，每台再在整张图上跑 Dijkstra。
